title: Tests fail on non-x86-64
body:
### Issue Description

Running `make -j1 localunit` fails on non-x86_64.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```
# https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/1164
export CGO_CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D_LARGEFILE64_SOURCE"

export BUILDTAGS="exclude_graphdriver_devicemapper seccomp apparmor libsqlite3"

make -j1 localunit
```

### Describe the results you received

Sample output from riscv64: https://gist.github.com/WhyNotHugo/9f40bc165d346261fd7deb1bd40384ba#file-gistfile1-txt

Most other architectures have almost identical output, except aarch64:

```
=== RUN   TestUnitDirs
    unitdirs_test.go:168: 
        	Error Trace:	go.podman.io/podman/v6/pkg/systemd/quadlet/unitdirs_test.go:168
        	Error:      	Received unexpected error:
        	            	fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted
        	Test:       	TestUnitDirs
--- FAIL: TestUnitDirs (0.00s)
FAIL
```

### Describe the results you expected

All tests should pass/skip on all architectures.

### podman info output

```yaml
n/a
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

None

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Running on Alpine Linux, attempting to enable tests during package builds.

### Additional information

n/a

comments.body: Right, `pkg/machine/os/ostree.go` is `//go:build amd64 || arm64`, but its tests run on all architectures.
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29712 fixes the more obvious bugs, but some of the other failures are beyond my understanding.

The compile issue is fixed so I assume `fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted` is the only failure you are left with?

This is a re-exec into a user namespace so my guess would be that user namesapces are not allowed in that environment where you run the tests
So, the test should check for user-namespace support and skip on `EPERM`.
I don’t see any kernel flag which can disable this behaviour, and our kernels are quite aligned across architectures. It’s not entirely clear to me why the test only fails on some architectures.
User namespaces are definitely enabled for us on all architectures.

Could you run these inside the environment where `TestUnitDirs` fails?
```bash
stat -c %i /              # inode != 2 means chroot
grep Seccomp /proc/self/status
unshare -U id             # does this work?
```

A reviewer has determined we need more information to understand the reported issue.  A comment on what is missing should be provided. Be certain you:

* provide an exact reproducer where possible
* verify you have provided all relevant information - minimum is `podman info`
* answer any follow up questions

If no response to the `needs-info` is provided in 30 days, this issue may be closed by our stale bot.

For more information on reporting issues on this repository, consult our [issue guide](ISSUE.md).
